procedure.method: Independent fresh editorial review. Read the exact pinned packet, case, review rules, rubric, compact method and addendum, and all five pinned native-evidence manifests before poster viewing; did not follow their unlisted embedded paths. The packet declares no source assets or protected layouts. Verified the pinned bytes and actual PNG header dimensions, separately from viewing. Used tools.view_image with detail original, forwarding each returned image through functions.exec image(), sequentially: R24-C1-M1 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M2 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M3 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M4 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M5 native, usage720, thumbnail320. All fifteen returned images were actually inspected in this order before the first copy-reading/transcription stage, judgment or score. After that complete sequence, read each Title and body in packet order from the already displayed native pixels, retaining observed line breaks, and assessed their usage and thumbnail presentations. No source opens were applicable, no view was unavailable, and no ambiguity-triggered revisit was necessary. No image creation/editing, replacement asset, peer review, maker inspection, spawn, fork or resume was used. These are semantic viewing attestations, not invented tool-event or session identifiers.

The hard black alley mass, receding ground marks, cream sky and tiny orange window build a continuous, quiet graphic street. The two-line serif-like Title overlaps M4 in typographic structure, but M4 painterly open sky and M5 enlarged print fragments have different image and emotional identities.

architectural frame and sky compared with M3

Broad brushwork, warm/cool painted walls and an upward sky opening convey bright domestic curiosity. M3 shares an alley subject and two-line Title but uses enclosed black silhouettes, a walked trail and a single warm point; their achieved identities remain clearly distinct.

residuals: Five distinct achieved identities are present, but diversity alone does not resolve M2 content specificity and its three below-floor ratings.

Shared four-line body wrapping is visible across the set, and M3/M4 share a two-line serif-like Title. These permitted reading-structure overlaps were assessed within each whole identity, not treated as a requirement for five different layouts.
